title.zh: 卷七十八 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫
title.en: Volume 78 Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun
title.raw: 卷七十八 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫 Volume 78 Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十八 蕭思話 劉延孫

translations.literal: Biographies 38: Xiao Sihua, Liu Yansun
translations.idiomatic: Biography 38: Xiao Sihua; Liu Yansun

sentences.zh: 蕭思話，南蘭陵人，孝懿皇后弟子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Sihua was a man of Nan Lanling and a nephew of Empress Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua was from Nan Lanling and was a nephew of Empress Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 父源之，字君流，歷中書黃門郎，徐、兗二州刺史，冠軍將軍、南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhi, style Junliu, served in succession as Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant, Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces, Champion General, and Administrator of Southern Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhi, courtesy name Junliu, had served as Secretariat Yellow Gate Attendant, governor of Xu and Yan provinces, Champion General, and administrator of Southern Langye.

sentences.zh: 永初元年卒，追贈前將軍。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yongchu and was posthumously enfeoffed as Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongchu 1 (420) and was posthumously given the rank of Forward General.

sentences.zh: 思話年十許歲，未知書，以博誕遊遨為事，好騎屋棟，打細腰鼓，侵暴鄰曲，莫不患毒之。

translations.literal: When Sihua was about ten years old he did not yet know books; he made gambling, debauchery, and roaming his occupation, liked riding along roof ridges and beating hourglass drums, and oppressed his neighbors—none did not suffer from him with loathing.
translations.idiomatic: At about ten years of age Sihua had not yet learned to read. He spent his days gambling, carousing, and roaming the streets—riding along roof ridges, beating hourglass drums, and bullying his neighbors until everyone in the district loathed him.

sentences.zh: 自此折節，數年中，遂有令譽。

translations.literal: From then on he restrained himself, and within several years came to have a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he reformed his conduct, and within a few years had earned an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 好書史，善彈琴，能騎射。

translations.literal: He loved books and histories, was skilled at playing the zither, and could ride and shoot.
translations.idiomatic: He took to books and history, became adept at the zither, and mastered horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 高祖一見，便以國器許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu saw him once, he thereby regarded him as a vessel of state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, upon meeting him once, declared him fit to be a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 年十八，除琅邪王大司馬行參軍，轉相國參軍，父憂去職。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he was appointed Acting Adjutant to the Grand Marshal of the Prince of Langye, transferred to be Adjutant to the Chancellor, and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was made acting adjutant to the Prince of Langye's grand marshal, then transferred to adjutant to the chancellor; he left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜羽林監，領石頭戍事，襲爵封陽縣侯，轉宣威將軍、彭城、沛二郡太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, charged with the garrison affairs of Stone City, inherited the fief as Marquis of Fengyang County, and was transferred to General Displaying Might, Administrator of Pengcheng and Pei commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended he was appointed supervisor of the imperial guard, took charge of the Stone City garrison, inherited the title Marquis of Fengyang, and was promoted to General Displaying Might with concurrent administration of Pengcheng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書傳，頗能隸書，解音律，便弓馬。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and commentaries, was quite able at clerical script, understood musical tones, and was handy with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories, wrote a fair hand in clerical script, understood music theory, and was skilled with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年，謝晦為荊州，欲請為司馬，思話拒之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanjia, when Xie Hui was in Jing Province, he wished to invite him as Chief of Staff, but Sihua refused.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 1 (424), when Xie Hui held Jing Province, he tried to recruit Sihua as his chief of staff, but Sihua declined.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷中書侍郎，仍督青州、徐州之東莞諸軍事、振武將軍、青州刺史，時年二十七。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman, and still supervised the military affairs of Dongguan in Qing and Xu Provinces, as General Quelling Wu and Inspector of Qing Province, at age twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 5 (428) he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and concurrently supervised military affairs in Dongguan (Qing and Xu), as General Quelling Wu and governor of Qing Province, at the age of twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 亡命司馬朗之、元之、可之兄弟，聚黨於東莞發干縣，謀為寇亂。

translations.literal: The outlaw brothers Sima Langzhi, Yuanzhi, and Kezhi gathered a faction at Fagan County in Dongguan and plotted to make bandit turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw brothers Sima Langzhi, Yuanzhi, and Kezhi rallied followers at Fagan in Dongguan and plotted a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 思話遣北海太守蕭汪之討斬之，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Sihua sent the Administrator of Beihai, Xiao Wangzhi, to attack and behead them; the remaining faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua sent Xiao Wangzhi, administrator of Beihai, to attack and execute them; the remaining rebels were all suppressed.

sentences.zh: 八年，除竟陵王義宣左軍司馬、南沛郡太守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Left Army Chief of Staff to Prince Jingling of Yixuan and Administrator of Southern Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 8 (431) he was appointed chief of staff to the Left Army of Prince Jingling Yixuan and administrator of Southern Pei.

sentences.zh: 未及就徵，索虜南寇，檀道濟北伐，既而回師，思話懼虜大至，乃棄鎮奔平昌。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the summons, the Northern Wei raided south; Tan Daoji marched north but then turned his army back. Sihua feared the barbarians would come in force and therefore abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could report to his new post, the Wei launched a southern raid. Tan Daoji marched north but soon withdrew; fearing a major Wei invasion, Sihua abandoned his command and fled to Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 思話先使參軍劉振之戍下邳，聞思話奔，亦委城走。

translations.literal: Sihua had earlier sent his adjutant Liu Zhenzhi to garrison Xiapi; hearing that Sihua had fled, he too abandoned the city and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had earlier posted his adjutant Liu Zhenzhi at Xiapi; when Liu heard of Sihua's flight, he too abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 虜定不至，而東陽積聚，已為百姓所焚，由是徵下廷尉，仍繫尚方。

translations.literal: The barbarians in the end did not arrive, but the stores at Dongyang had already been burned by the common people; on this account he was summoned down to the Court of Justice and still imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army never came, but the grain stores at Dongyang had already been burned by local people. For this he was summoned to the Court of Justice and imprisoned in the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 初在青州，常所用銅鬥，覆在藥廚下，得二死雀，思話曰：「鬥覆而雙雀殞，其不祥乎！

translations.literal: Earlier when he was in Qing Province, a copper dipper he commonly used lay overturned beneath the medicine cupboard, and two dead sparrows were found. Sihua said: "The dipper overturned and twin sparrows perished—is this not inauspicious!"
translations.idiomatic: While he was in Qing Province, a copper dipper he often used was found overturned under the medicine cupboard with two dead sparrows beneath it. Sihua said, "The dipper overturned and two sparrows died—is this not an ill omen?"

sentences.zh: 」既而被繫。

translations.literal: " Shortly after he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 九年，仇池大饑，益、梁州豐稔，梁州刺史甄法護在任失和，氐帥楊難當因此寇漢中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Chouchi suffered great famine while Yi and Liang Provinces had abundant harvests. The Inspector of Liang Province, Zhen Fahu, lost harmony in his tenure, and the Di chieftain Yang Nandang therefore raided Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 9 (432), Chouchi suffered famine while Yi and Liang provinces enjoyed good harvests. Zhen Fahu, governor of Liang, had lost the loyalty of his subjects, and the Di chieftain Yang Nandang seized the opportunity to invade Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乃自徒中起思話督梁、南秦二州諸軍事、橫野將軍、梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon from among the convicts they raised Sihua to supervise the military affairs of Liang and Southern Qin Provinces, as General of Wide Conquest and Inspector of Liang and Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The court then raised Sihua from among the convicts to supervise military affairs in Liang and Southern Qin, as General of Wide Conquest and governor of both provinces.

sentences.zh: 既行，聞法護已委鎮北奔西城，遣司馬、建威將軍、南漢中太守蕭諱五百人前進；

translations.literal: After he set out, he heard that Fahu had already abandoned his post and fled north to Xicheng. He sent his Chief of Staff, General Establishing Might, and Administrator of Southern Hanzhong, Xiao Hui, with five hundred men to advance first;
translations.idiomatic: On the march he learned that Fahu had abandoned his post and fled north to Xicheng. He sent his chief of staff Xiao Hui—General Establishing Might and administrator of Southern Hanzhong—with five hundred men ahead;

sentences.zh: 又遣西戎長史蕭汪之係之。

translations.literal: and also sent the Western Rong Chief Clerk Xiao Wangzhi to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Western Rong chief clerk Xiao Wangzhi to follow in support.

sentences.zh: 諱緣路收合士眾，得精兵千人。

translations.literal: Hui along the way gathered soldiers and obtained a thousand elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route Hui gathered troops and mustered a thousand elite soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，進據磝頭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year he advanced and occupied Qiaotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanjia 10 (433) he advanced and took Qiaotou.

sentences.zh: 難當焚掠漢中，引眾西還，留其輔國將軍、梁秦二州刺史趙溫守梁州，魏興太守薛健據黃金。

translations.literal: Nandang burned and plundered Hanzhong, led his masses westward back, left his Assistant State General and Inspector of Liang and Qin, Zhao Wen, to hold Liang Province, and the Administrator of Weixing, Xue Jian, held Huangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang burned and looted Hanzhong, then withdrew west, leaving his Assistant State General Zhao Wen—governor of Liang and Qin—to hold Liang Province while Weixing administrator Xue Jian occupied Huangjin.

sentences.zh: 諱進屯磝頭，遣陰平太守蕭坦赴黃金，薛健副薑寶據鐵城，鐵城與黃金相對，去一裏，斫樹塞道。

translations.literal: Hui advanced and encamped at Qiaotou, sent the Administrator of Yinping, Xiao Tan, toward Huangjin. Xue Jian's deputy Jiang Bao held Tiecheng; Tiecheng faced Huangjin across one li, and they felled trees to block the road.
translations.idiomatic: Hui advanced to Qiaotou and sent Yinping administrator Xiao Tan against Huangjin. Xue Jian's deputy Jiang Bao held Tiecheng, a fortress facing Huangjin across one li; the defenders felled trees to block the road.

sentences.zh: 坦進攻二戍，拔之。

translations.literal: Tan advanced to attack the two garrisons and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan attacked both garrisons and took them.

sentences.zh: 二月，趙溫又率薛健及其寧朔將軍、馮翼太守蒲早子來攻坦營，坦奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhao Wen again led Xue Jian and his General Pacifying the North, Administrator of Fengyi Pu Zaozi, to attack Tan's camp; Tan struck fiercely and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Zhao Wen led Xue Jian, General Pacifying the North Pu Zaozi of Fengyi, and others against Tan's camp; Tan counterattacked fiercely and routed them.

sentences.zh: 坦被創，賊退保西水。

translations.literal: Tan was wounded; the rebels withdrew to hold Xishui.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was wounded; the enemy fell back to defend Xishui.

sentences.zh: 諱司馬錫文祖進據黃金，蕭汪之步騎五百相繼而至。

translations.literal: Hui's Chief Clerk Xi Wenzu advanced and occupied Huangjin; Xiao Wangzhi's five hundred infantry and cavalry arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's chief clerk Xi Wenzu advanced to Huangjin, and Xiao Wangzhi's five hundred infantry and cavalry arrived in succession.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍臨川王義慶遣龍驤將軍裴方明三千人赴，諱等進黃金，早子、健等退保下桃。

translations.literal: The General Pacifying the West, Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, sent the General of the Dragon Cavalry Pei Fangming with three thousand men to go; Hui and others advanced on Huangjin, and Zaozi, Jian, and others withdrew to hold Xiatao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, General Pacifying the West, sent General of the Dragon Cavalry Pei Fangming with three thousand men to reinforce them. Hui and his forces advanced on Huangjin; Zaozi, Jian, and the others fell back to Xiatao.

sentences.zh: 思話先遣行參軍王靈濟率偏軍出洋川，因向南城。

translations.literal: Sihua had earlier sent the Acting Adjutant Wang Lingji leading a detached army out from Yangchuan, and thereby toward Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua had earlier sent acting adjutant Wang Lingji with a detached force from Yangchuan toward Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 偽陵江將軍趙英堅守險，靈濟擊破之，生禽英。

translations.literal: The false General Guarding the River Zhao Ying held the passes firmly; Lingji attacked and defeated him, capturing Ying alive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Zhao Ying held the mountain passes; Lingji defeated him and took Ying alive.

sentences.zh: 南城空虛，因資無所，復引軍還與諱合。

translations.literal: Nancheng was empty; there was nowhere to draw supplies, so he again led the army back to join Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Nancheng was empty and offered no supplies, so he withdrew to rejoin Hui.

sentences.zh: 三月，諱率眾軍進據峨公固。

translations.literal: In the third month, Hui led the mass of armies forward and occupied Egonggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hui led the combined armies forward and occupied Egonggu.

sentences.zh: 難當遣其子和率趙溫、蒲早子及左衛將軍呂平、寧朔將軍司馬飛龍，步騎萬餘，跨漢津結柴，其間立浮橋，悉力攻諱，合圍數十重，短兵接戰，弓矢無復用。

translations.literal: Nandang sent his son He leading Zhao Wen, Pu Zaozi, and the Left Guard General Lü Ping and General Pacifying the North Sima Feilong, with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry. They crossed the Han ford and built stockades, set a pontoon bridge between them, and with full force attacked Hui, surrounding him in dozens of rings; they fought at close quarters and bows and arrows were no longer of use.
translations.idiomatic: Nandang sent his son He with Zhao Wen, Pu Zaozi, Left Guard General Lü Ping, General Pacifying the North Sima Feilong, and more than ten thousand foot and horse. They crossed the Han ford, built stockades, and threw a pontoon bridge across; then they threw their full strength against Hui, surrounding him in layer upon layer until the fight became hand-to-hand and bows and arrows were useless.

sentences.zh: 賊悉衣犀革，戈矛所不能加。

translations.literal: The rebels all wore rhinoceros hide; spears and halberds could not pierce them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy all wore rhinoceros-hide armor that spears and halberds could not penetrate.

sentences.zh: 諱乃截矟長數尺，以大斧椎之，一矟輒貫十餘賊。

translations.literal: Hui then cut spears to several feet in length and drove them with great axes; one spear would pierce through more than ten rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had spears cut to several feet and driven in with heavy axes; a single thrust would run through more than ten men.

sentences.zh: 賊不能當，因大敗，燒柴奔走，退據大桃。

translations.literal: The rebels could not withstand it and were thereby greatly defeated; they burned the stockades and fled, withdrawing to hold Datao.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy could not hold; they were routed, burned their stockades, and fled to Datao.

sentences.zh: 閏月，諱及方明臺軍至，龍驤將軍楊平興、幢主殿中將軍梁坦直入角弩追之，賊又敗走，殺傷虜獲甚多。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Hui and Fangming's allied armies arrived; the General of the Dragon Cavalry Yang Pingxing and the standard-bearer Palace Attendant General Liang Tan pressed in with corner-mounted crossbows in pursuit; the rebels were again defeated and fled, with many killed, wounded, captured, and booty taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Hui and Fangming's allied forces arrived. General of the Dragon Cavalry Yang Pingxing and standard-bearer Palace Attendant General Liang Tan pressed the pursuit with corner-mounted crossbows; the enemy was routed again, with heavy casualties and captures.

sentences.zh: 漢中平，悉收沒地，置戍葭萌水。

translations.literal: Hanzhong was pacified; all lost territory was recovered and garrisons were set at Jiameng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong was pacified; all lost territory was recovered and garrisons established at Jiameng Ford.

sentences.zh: 先是，桓玄篡晉，以桓希為梁州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped Jin, he appointed Huan Xi as Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huan Xuan usurped the Jin throne, he appointed Huan Xi governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 布敗走，氐楊盛據有漢中，刺史范元之、傅歆悉治魏興，唯得魏興、上庸、新城三郡。

translations.literal: Bu was defeated and fled; the Di Yang Sheng seized Hanzhong. The inspectors Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin both administered from Weixing, obtaining only the three commanderies of Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bu was defeated and fled; the Di chieftain Yang Sheng seized Hanzhong. Governors Fan Yuanzhi and Fu Xin both ruled from Weixing, holding only Weixing, Shangyong, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 其後索邈為刺史，乃治南城。

translations.literal: After that Suo Miao became inspector and then administered from Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later Suo Miao became governor and moved the seat to Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 為賊所焚燒不可固，即思話遷鎮南域，加節，進號寧朔將軍，征諱為太子屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: It had been burned by rebels and could not be held firm; thereupon Sihua moved his headquarters to the southern region, was given the staff of authority, advanced in rank to General Pacifying the North, and Hui was summoned as Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The city had been burned by the enemy and could not be held; Sihua moved his headquarters to the southern region, received the staff of authority, was promoted to General Pacifying the North, and Hui was summoned to serve as colonel of the heir apparent's garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 法護，中山無極人，過江寓居南郡。

translations.literal: Fahu was a man of Wuji in Zhongshan; after crossing the river he lodged in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was from Wuji in Zhongshan; after crossing south of the Yangzi he settled in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟法崇，元嘉十年，自少府為益州刺史。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fachong, in the tenth year of Yuanjia, went from Minister of the Privy Purse to Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fachong, in Yuanjia 10 (433), moved from Minister of the Privy Purse to governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 法護委鎮之罪，統府所收，於獄賜死。

translations.literal: Fahu's crime of abandoning his post was taken in by the chief commandery office; he was granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fahu was tried for abandoning his post by the chief commandery office and ordered to take his own life in prison.

sentences.zh: 太祖以法崇受任一方，令獄官言法護病卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu, because Fachong was entrusted with a region, ordered the prison officials to say that Fahu had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fachong held a provincial post, Emperor Taizu had the prison officials report that Fahu had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 太祖使思話上平定漢中本末，下之史官。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu had Sihua submit the full account of pacifying Hanzhong and sent it down to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Sihua submit a full report on the pacification of Hanzhong and forwarded it to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷使持節、臨川王義慶平西長史、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Chief Clerk Pacifying the West to Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, and Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 14 (437) he was transferred to bearer of the staff, chief clerk pacifying the west under Prince of Linchuan Yiqing, and colonel of the southern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 太祖賜以弓琴，手敕曰：「丈人頃何所作？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu bestowed on him a bow and zither, with a personal edict saying: "Elder, what have you been doing lately?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a bow and a zither with a personal note: "Elder, what have you been up to lately?"

sentences.zh: 事務之暇，故以琴書為娛耳，所得不曰義邪！

translations.literal: In the leisure from official business, I therefore take zither and books as amusement—is what one gains not called righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals between duties I take the zither and books for amusement—is that not a worthy pursuit?

sentences.zh: 眷想常不忘情，想亦同之。

translations.literal: My affectionate thoughts never forget feeling; I think you feel the same.
translations.idiomatic: My affection for you never fades; I trust you feel the same.

sentences.zh: 前得此琴，云是舊物，亦有名京邑，今以相借。

translations.literal: I recently obtained this zither, which is said to be an old piece and also had a name in the capital; now I lend it to you.
translations.idiomatic: I recently acquired this zither—said to be an antique once famous in the capital—and now lend it to you.

sentences.zh: 因是戴顒意於彈撫，響韻殊勝，直爾嘉也。

translations.literal: Because Dai Yong was skilled at playing it, its tone and resonance were especially superior—truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yong played it with such skill that its tone was superb—truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 並往桑弓一張，材理乃快，先所常用，既久廢射，又多病，略不能制之，便成老公，令人歎息。

translations.literal: Also sent is one mulberry bow; its grain is quite lively—it was what I commonly used before. Having long abandoned archery and being much afflicted by illness, I can scarcely draw it anymore and have become an old man—this makes one sigh.
translations.idiomatic: I also send a mulberry bow of fine grain that I once used often. I have long given up archery and am much afflicted by illness; I can scarcely draw it now and have become an old man—it is lamentable.

sentences.zh: 良材美器，宜在盡用之地，丈人真無所與讓也。」

translations.literal: Fine timber and beautiful instruments ought to be in a place where they are fully used—you, elder, truly have nothing to yield to others."
translations.idiomatic: Fine timber and beautiful instruments belong where they will be fully used—you, elder, should accept them without demur."

sentences.zh: 十六年，衡陽王義季代義慶，又除安西長史，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, he was again appointed Chief Clerk Pacifying the West; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 16 (439), when Prince of Hengyang Yiji replaced Yiqing, Sihua was again appointed chief clerk pacifying the west; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 十九年，徵為侍中，領前軍將軍，未就徵，復先職。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was summoned as Palace Attendant and concurrently Forward Army General; before he could take up the summons he returned to his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 19 (442) he was summoned as palace attendant and Forward Army General, but before he could report he was restored to his former posts.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷持節、監雍州、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之南陽、竟陵、順陽、襄陽、新野、隨六郡諸軍事、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, overseeing the military affairs of Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin Provinces and the six commanderies of Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui in Jing Province, as Colonel Pacifying the Man, Inspector of Yong Province, and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made bearer of the staff, overseeing military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin, and six Jing commanderies (Nanyang, Jingling, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Sui), as colonel pacifying the barbarians, governor of Yong, and administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除侍中，領太子右率。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 22 (445) he was appointed palace attendant and right leader of the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，改領左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was changed to concurrently Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 24 (447) he was transferred to Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 嘗從太祖登鍾山北嶺，中道有磐石清泉，上使於石上彈琴，因賜以銀鍾酒，謂曰：「相賞有松石間意。

translations.literal: He once followed Emperor Taizu in climbing the northern ridge of Zhongshan; midway there was a boulder and clear spring. The emperor had him play the zither on the stone and thereby bestowed silver-bell wine on him, saying: "In mutual appreciation there is the mood of pines and rocks."
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying Emperor Taizu up the northern slope of Zhongshan, they came upon a boulder beside a clear spring. The emperor had him play the zither on the rock and rewarded him with silver-bell wine, saying, "We share the spirit of pines and stones."

sentences.zh: 」又領南徐州大中正。

translations.literal: " He also concurrently held the post of Chief Rectifier of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He also served as chief rectifier of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 明年，復監雍、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、右將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史如故。

translations.literal: The next year he again oversaw the military affairs of Yong, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin and the two commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Jing Province, as Right General, Colonel Pacifying the Man, and Inspector of Yong Province as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again oversaw Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin, and the Jing commanderies of Jingling and Sui, as Right General, colonel pacifying the barbarians, and governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，徵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was summoned as Minister of the Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 26 (449) he was summoned as Minister of the Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 詔思話曰：「沈尚書暴病不救，其體業貞審，立朝盡公，年時尚可，方相委任，奄忽不永，痛惋特深。

translations.literal: An edict to Sihua said: "Minister Shen died suddenly beyond saving. His conduct and achievement were upright and careful; in court he was wholly public-minded. His years were still acceptable and he was just being entrusted—suddenly he was not long-lived; grief and regret are especially deep."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Sihua read: "Minister Shen died suddenly, beyond help. Upright and conscientious in office, wholly devoted to the public good, still in his prime and just entrusted with heavy duties—gone so suddenly. Our grief is profound."

sentences.zh: 銓管要機，通塞所寄，丈人才用體國，二三惟允。

translations.literal: The selection and control of key mechanisms is what prosperity and obstruction depend on; you, elder, have talent and ability that embody the state—of two or three men, you alone are fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The selection of officials is vital to the state's fortunes; you, elder, have the talent to serve the realm—among the few fit for this post, you are foremost."

sentences.zh: 」思話以去州無復事力，倩府軍身九人，太祖戲之曰：「丈人終不為田父于裏閭，何應無人使邪？

translations.literal: " Sihua, because leaving the province he no longer had staff at his disposal, borrowed nine men from the princely establishment's military household. Emperor Taizu jested with him, saying: "You, elder, are after all not a farmer in the lanes—how should you have no one to send?"
translations.idiomatic: " Having left his province without retainers, Sihua borrowed nine men from the princely household guard. The emperor teased him: "Surely you are no village farmer, elder—how can you have no attendants?"

sentences.zh: 」未拜，二十七年，遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Before he took up the appointment, in the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to General Protecting the Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could take up the post, in Yuanjia 27 (450) he was transferred to General Protecting the Army.

sentences.zh: 是年春，虜攻懸瓠，太祖將大舉北討，朝士僉同，莫或異議。

translations.literal: That spring the barbarians attacked Xuanhu; Emperor Taizu was about to launch a great northern campaign. The court gentlemen were all of one voice, and none had a differing opinion.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the Wei attacked Xuanhu; the emperor planned a major northern campaign. The court was unanimous—no one dissented.

sentences.zh: 思話固諫，不從。

translations.literal: Sihua firmly remonstrated but was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua remonstrated firmly, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 乃領精甲三千，助鎮彭城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led three thousand elite armored troops to help garrison Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then led three thousand elite armored troops to help defend Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 虜退，即代世祖為持節、監徐、兗、青、冀四州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、撫軍將軍、兗、徐二州刺史。

translations.literal: When the barbarians withdrew, he immediately replaced Emperor Shizu as Bearer of the Staff, overseeing the military affairs of Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji Provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, as General Soothing the Army and Inspector of Yan and Xu Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei withdrew, he replaced Emperor Xiaowu as bearer of the staff, overseeing Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji and Liang in Yu, as General Soothing the Army and governor of Yan and Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，統揚武將軍、冀州刺史張永眾軍圍碻磝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he commanded the mass of armies under General Displaying Martiality and Inspector of Ji Province Zhang Yong to besiege Quecheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 29 (452) he commanded the armies under Zhang Yong, General Displaying Martiality and governor of Ji, in the siege of Quecheng.

sentences.zh: 初，鎮軍諮議參軍申坦與王玄謨圍滑臺，不克，免官。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Consulting Adjutant to the General Stabilizing the Army Shen Tan, with Wang Xuamo, besieged Huatai but did not take it and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, consulting adjutant Shen Tan had joined Wang Xuamo in besieging Huatai without success and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史蕭斌板坦行建威將軍、濟南平原二郡太守，守歷城，令任仲仁又為坦副，並前鋒入河。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Qing Province Xiao Bin appointed Tan acting General Establishing Might and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan commanderies, to hold Licheng, and made Ren Zhongren Tan's deputy; both were vanguard forces entering the river region.
translations.idiomatic: Qing governor Xiao Bin appointed Tan acting General Establishing Might and administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan, to hold Licheng, with Ren Zhongren as his deputy; both led the vanguard into the Yellow River region.

sentences.zh: 五月，發沿口，永司馬崔訓、建武將軍齊郡太守胡景世率青州軍來會。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they set out from Yankou; Yong's Chief of Staff Cui Xun and General Establishing Martiality and Administrator of Qi commandery Hu Jingshi led the Qing army to join.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they set out from Yankou; Zhang Yong's chief of staff Cui Xun and General Establishing Martiality Hu Jingshi, administrator of Qi, led the Qing forces to join them.

sentences.zh: 七月，思話及眾軍並至碻磝，治三攻道。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Sihua and the mass of armies all reached Quecheng and constructed three assault approaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Sihua and the combined armies reached Quecheng and built three assault ramps.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣員外散騎侍郎徐爰宣旨督戰。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu sent the Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Xu Ai to proclaim the imperial will and supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent extraordinary gentleman of the scattered cavalry Xu Ai to convey the imperial will and supervise operations.

sentences.zh: 張永、胡景世當東攻道，申坦、任仲仁西攻道，崔訓南攻道。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong and Hu Jingshi were assigned the eastern assault approach; Shen Tan and Ren Zhongren the western; Cui Xun the southern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Hu Jingshi took the eastern ramp; Shen Tan and Ren Zhongren the western; Cui Xun the southern.

sentences.zh: 賊夜地道出，燒崔訓樓及蟆車，又燒胡景世樓及攻具，尋又毀崔訓攻道，城不可拔。

translations.literal: The rebels came out by tunnel at night and burned Cui Xun's tower and toad-carts, also burned Hu Jingshi's tower and siege equipment, and soon afterward destroyed Cui Xun's assault approach; the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy tunneled out by night and burned Cui Xun's siege tower and assault vehicles, then Hu Jingshi's tower and equipment; they soon destroyed Cui Xun's ramp as well, and the city could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 思話馳來，退師。

translations.literal: Sihua came at full gallop and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua rode up in haste and ordered a withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 攻城凡十八日，解圍還歷下。

translations.literal: The siege of the city lasted eighteen days in all; they lifted the encirclement and returned to Lixia.
translations.idiomatic: After eighteen days of siege they lifted the encirclement and withdrew to Lixia.

sentences.zh: 崔訓以樓見燒，又不能固攻道，被誅於碻磝；

translations.literal: Cui Xun, because his tower was seen burned and he also could not secure the assault approach, was executed at Quecheng;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xun was executed at Quecheng because his siege tower had been burned and he had failed to hold the assault ramp;

sentences.zh: 永、坦並繫獄。

translations.literal: Yong and Tan were both imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong and Shen Tan were both imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「得撫軍將軍思話啟事，碻磝不拔，士卒疲勞，且班師清濟，更圖進討。

translations.literal: An edict said: "We have received the memorial of General Soothing the Army Sihua: Quecheng cannot be taken, the soldiers and officers are weary—for the present withdraw the army to clear the Ji River and plan another advance."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "We have received General Soothing the Army Sihua's report: Quecheng cannot be taken and the troops are exhausted—for now withdraw to the Ji River and plan a new advance."

sentences.zh: 此鎮山川嚴阻，控臨河朔，形勝之要，擅名自古，宜除其授，以允望實。

translations.literal: This fortress has mountains and rivers stern and obstructed, controlling and overlooking the north of the river—a strategic key renowned from antiquity; its commission should be removed to fulfill expectations and reality.
translations.idiomatic: This fortress lies in rugged terrain commanding the north bank of the Yellow River—a strategic choke point famed since antiquity. Its garrison command should be reorganized to match its importance.

sentences.zh: 思話可解徐州為冀州，餘如故。

translations.literal: Sihua may relinquish Xu Province for Ji Province; the rest remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua shall exchange Xu for Ji Province; his other posts remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 彭城文武，復量分配，即鎮歷城。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials of Pengcheng are to be reassessed and redistributed; he is immediately to garrison Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military staff of Pengcheng are to be reassigned, and he shall immediately take up his post at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 」尋為江夏王義恭所奏，免官。

translations.literal: " Shortly after he was impeached by Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Prince of Jiangxia Yigong impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以為使持節、監徐、青、兗、冀四州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、徐、兗二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When the usurper murdered and enthroned himself, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, overseeing the military affairs of Xu, Qing, Yan, and Ji Provinces and Liang commandery in Yu Province, and Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Liu Shao seized the throne, Sihua was appointed bearer of the staff, overseeing Xu, Qing, Yan, and Ji and Liang in Yu, and governor of Xu and Yan; his general's rank was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 思話即率部曲還彭城，起義以應世祖。

translations.literal: Sihua immediately led his household troops back to Pengcheng and raised righteous arms to respond to Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua immediately led his household troops back to Pengcheng and rose in support of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 遣使奉箋曰：「下官近在歷下，始奉國諱，所承使人，不知闊狹，既還在路，漸有所聞，猶謂人倫無容有此，私懷感慨，未敢在言。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger presenting a memorial saying: "Your subordinate was recently at Lixia and had just received the national mourning taboo. The envoy I received did not know breadth or narrowness; already on the return road I gradually heard something, yet still thought human relations could not permit this—I privately harbored emotion and did not dare speak openly."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger with a memorial: "Your servant was recently at Lixia when the national mourning was proclaimed. The envoy who reached me gave no clear account; on the road back I began to hear rumors, yet still could not believe that human decency could permit such a thing—I grieved in private and dared not speak openly."

sentences.zh: 奉被今教，果出慮表，重增哀惋，不能自勝。

translations.literal: Having received your present instruction, it truly exceeded what I had feared, redoubling grief and regret—I cannot overcome myself.
translations.idiomatic: Your present command confirms what I had dreaded, deepening my grief beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 此實天地所不覆載，人神所不容忍，率土民氓，莫不憤咽，況下官蒙荷榮渥，義兼常志。

translations.literal: This truly is what Heaven and Earth do not cover and sustain, what men and spirits cannot endure—all the people within the realm, none do not choke with rage; how much more your subordinate, who has received grace and favor, with righteousness joined to ordinary resolve.
translations.idiomatic: This is an outrage that Heaven and Earth cannot shelter and that gods and men cannot abide—all within the realm choke with rage; how much more your servant, who has received the court's grace and owes it a loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 此月五日，被驛使追命騎還朝，切齒拊心，輒已鍾疾，雖百口在都，一非所顧。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of this month I was pursued by post-station envoys ordering me to ride back to court; I gnash my teeth and beat my breast and have already been stricken with illness—though a hundred mouths are in the capital, not one is what I consider.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth of this month post-riders summoned me back to court. I gnash my teeth and clutch my heart, already stricken with grief—though my whole family is in the capital, I think of nothing but this outrage.

sentences.zh: 正欲遣啟受規略，會奉今旨，悲懼兼情。

translations.literal: I was just about to send a dispatch to receive your strategic plan when I met your present command—grief and fear mingled in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I was about to send a dispatch asking for your strategy when your command arrived—grief and fear overwhelmed me together.

sentences.zh: 伏承司徒英圖電發，殿下神武霜斷，臧質忠義並到，不謀同時，仗順沿流，席捲江甸，前驅風邁，已應在近。

translations.literal: I bow and receive that the Minister's heroic plan flashes forth like lightning, Your Highness's divine martial prowess cuts like frost, Zang Zhi's loyalty and righteousness have both arrived without plotting together—relying on righteousness they follow the current, rolling up the river districts like a mat; the vanguard wind-swift should already be near.
translations.idiomatic: I learn that the Minister's grand design moves like lightning, that Your Highness's martial resolve is sharp as frost, that Zang Zhi's loyal forces have joined you without prior arrangement—riding the tide of righteousness down the Yangzi, sweeping the river districts; your vanguard should already be near at hand.

sentences.zh: 下官復練始集，遣輔國將軍申坦、龍驤將軍梁坦二軍，分配精甲五千，申坦為統，便以即日水陸齊下。

translations.literal: Your subordinate has again gathered and drilled the troops just assembled, sending the two armies of General Assisting the State Shen Tan and General of the Dragon Cavalry Liang Tan, allotting five thousand elite armored men with Shen Tan as commander—they shall on this very day descend together by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has mustered his forces anew and sends the armies of General Assisting the State Shen Tan and General of the Dragon Cavalry Liang Tan with five thousand elite armored troops under Shen Tan's command—they will march downriver by land and water this very day.

sentences.zh: 下官悉率文武，駱驛繼發。

translations.literal: Your subordinate will lead all civil and military officials in relays without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant will lead all his civil and military officers in rapid succession.

sentences.zh: 憑威策懦，勢同振朽，開泰有期，悲欣交集。

translations.literal: Relying on your might to drive the timid, the momentum is like shaking rotten wood; the opening of great peace has its season—grief and joy intermingle.
translations.idiomatic: With your authority driving the timid, our momentum will be like shaking rotten timber; peace is within reach—grief and joy mingle in my heart.

sentences.zh: 」世祖至新亭，坦亦進克京口。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Tan also advanced and captured Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Xiaojian, at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xiaojian 2 (455) at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 追贈征西將軍、開府儀同三司，持節、常侍、都督、刺史如故，諡曰穆侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as General Campaigning West and Grand Master with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes; Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief, and Inspector remained as before; his posthumous title was Marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Campaigning West and grand master with ceremonies equal to the three dukes; his staff, regular attendant, commander-in-chief, and inspector posts were unchanged; his posthumous title was Marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 思話宗戚令望，蚤見任待，凡歷州十二，杖節監都督九焉。

translations.literal: Sihua was of eminent clan and kin with fine reputation, early seen and entrusted; in all he passed through twelve provinces and bore the staff in oversight and command nine times.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua came from a distinguished clan with an excellent reputation and was entrusted early in life; he governed twelve provinces in all and nine times bore the staff of command.

sentences.zh: 所至雖無皦皦清節，亦無穢黷之累。

translations.literal: Where he went, though he had no dazzling purity of conduct, he also had no stain of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Though nowhere he served was he noted for dazzling integrity, neither did he leave a record of corruption.

sentences.zh: 愛才好士，人多歸之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and honored scholars; many men attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent and honored scholars, and many men gathered under him.

sentences.zh: 長子惠開嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His eldest son Huikai succeeded him; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Huikai succeeded him and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 次子惠明，亦有世譽，歷黃門郎，御史中丞，司徒左長史，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His second son Huiming also had a reputation in the age, serving in succession as Yellow Gate Gentleman, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State, and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Huiming also enjoyed a fine reputation, serving as yellow gate gentleman, imperial censor-in-chief, left chief clerk of the minister of state, and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽末，卒官。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the end of the Yuanhui era under Emperor Houfei.

sentences.zh: 第四子惠基，順帝昇明末，為侍中。

translations.literal: His fourth son Huiji, at the end of Shengming under Emperor Shun, was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His fourth son Huiji became palace attendant at the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 源之從父弟摹之，丹陽尹，追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi's paternal cousin Mozhi was Intendant of Danyang and was posthumously enfeoffed as General Campaigning against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi's paternal cousin Mozhi served as intendant of Danyang and was posthumously made General Campaigning against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 子斌，亦為太祖所遇。

translations.literal: His son Bin was also favored by Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin was also favored by Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康鎮豫章，以為大將軍諮議參軍、豫章太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang garrisoned Yuzhang, he was made Consulting Adjutant to the Grand General and Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Pengcheng Yikang held Yuzhang, Bin was made consulting adjutant to the grand general and administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歷南蠻校尉，侍中，輔國將軍、青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Colonel of the Southern Man, Palace Attendant, General Assisting the State, and Inspector of Qing and Ji Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as colonel of the southern barbarians, palace attendant, General Assisting the State, and governor of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，統王玄謨等眾軍北伐。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he commanded the mass of armies under Wang Xuamo and others in the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 27 (450) he commanded the armies under Wang Xuamo and others in the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 斌遣將軍崔猛攻虜青州刺史張淮之於樂安，淮之棄城走。

translations.literal: Bin sent the general Cui Meng to attack the barbarians' Inspector of Qing Province Zhang Huaizhi at Le'an; Huaizhi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent General Cui Meng to attack the Wei governor of Qing, Zhang Huaizhi, at Le'an; Huaizhi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 先是，猛與斌參軍傅融分取樂安及碻磝，樂安水道不通，先並定碻磝，至是又克樂安。

translations.literal: Earlier, Meng and Bin's adjutant Fu Rong had divided the taking of Le'an and Quecheng; the water route to Le'an was not open, so they first together secured Quecheng; at this time they again took Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Meng and Bin's adjutant Fu Rong had divided the tasks of taking Le'an and Quecheng; the water route to Le'an was blocked, so they secured Quecheng first; now they took Le'an as well.

sentences.zh: 既而攻圍滑臺，不拔。

translations.literal: Thereafter they attacked and besieged Huatai but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Huatai but could not take it.

sentences.zh: 斌追還歷下，事在王玄謨傳。

translations.literal: Bin pursued back to Lixia; the matter is in the biography of Wang Xuamo.
translations.idiomatic: Bin withdrew to Lixia; the full account is in Wang Xuamo's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，亡命司馬順則詐稱晉室近屬，自號齊王，聚眾據梁鄒城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the outlaw Sima Shunze falsely claimed to be a close kin of the Jin house, styled himself King of Qi, gathered a crowd, and held Liangzou city.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 28 (451) the outlaw Sima Shunze falsely claimed kinship with the Jin imperial house, proclaimed himself King of Qi, rallied followers, and seized Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 又有沙門自稱司馬百年，號安定王，亡命秦凱之、祖元明等各據村屯以應順則。

translations.literal: There was also a monk who called himself Sima Bainian and styled himself King of Anding; the outlaws Qin Kaizhi, Zu Yuanming, and others each held village stockades to respond to Shunze.
translations.idiomatic: A monk also called himself Sima Bainian and styled himself King of Anding; outlaws Qin Kaizhi, Zu Yuanming, and others held village strongholds in support of Shunze.

sentences.zh: 初，梁鄒戍主、宣威將軍、樂安、渤海二郡太守崔勳之出州，故順則因虛竊據。

translations.literal: Earlier, the garrison commander of Liangzou, General Displaying Might, and Administrator of Le'an and Bohai commanderies Cui Xunzhi had left the province, so Shunze took advantage of the vacancy to seize it secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Liangzou garrison commander Cui Xunzhi—General Displaying Might and administrator of Le'an and Bohai—had left the province, allowing Shunze to seize the city in his absence.

sentences.zh: 勳之司馬曹敬會拒戰不敵，出走。

translations.literal: Xunzhi's Chief of Staff Cao Jinghui resisted battle but could not match them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi's chief of staff Cao Jinghui fought but was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 斌即遣勳之率行建威將軍濟南、平原二郡太守申坦、長流參軍羅文昌等諸軍討順則，攻之不克。

translations.literal: Bin immediately sent Xunzhi leading the acting General Establishing Might and Administrator of Jinan and Pingyuan Shen Tan, the Long-Service Adjutant Luo Wenchang, and other armies to suppress Shunze; they attacked but could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Bin immediately sent Xunzhi with acting General Establishing Might Shen Tan of Jinan and Pingyuan, long-service adjutant Luo Wenchang, and other forces against Shunze, but the attack failed.

sentences.zh: 勳之等始謂城內出於逼附，軍至即應奔逃，而並為賊堅守，殺傷官軍甚多。

translations.literal: Xunzhi and the others at first thought those inside the city had joined under compulsion and that when the army arrived they would surely flee; instead they all held firm for the rebels and killed and wounded many government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi and his officers had assumed the townspeople joined under duress and would flee when the army arrived; instead the rebels held firm and inflicted heavy casualties on the government forces.

sentences.zh: 斌又遣府司馬、建武將軍、齊郡太守龐秀之總諸軍。

translations.literal: Bin again sent the princely establishment's Chief of Staff, General Establishing Martiality, and Administrator of Qi commandery Pang Xiuzhi to command all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Bin then sent his chief of staff Pang Xiuzhi—General Establishing Martiality and administrator of Qi—to take overall command.

sentences.zh: 祖元明又據安丘城，斌更遣振武將軍劉武之及軍主劉回精兵千人，討司馬百年，斬之。

translations.literal: Zu Yuanming again held Anqiu city; Bin further sent General Quelling Wu Liu Wuzhi and the army commander Liu Hui with a thousand elite troops to suppress Sima Bainian and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Yuanming also held Anqiu; Bin sent General Quelling Wu Liu Wuzhi and army commander Liu Hui with a thousand elite troops against Sima Bainian and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 順則既失據，眾稍離阻。

translations.literal: Once Shunze had lost his foothold, the masses gradually dispersed and obstructed no more.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shunze lost his base, his followers gradually dispersed.

sentences.zh: 文昌遣道連偽投賊，賊信納之，潛以官賞格示眾，城內賊黨李繼叔等並有歸順心。

translations.literal: Wenchang sent Dao Lian to feign surrender to the rebels; the rebels trusted and accepted him. He secretly showed the crowd the government's reward schedule; inside the city the rebel faction Li Jishu and others all had hearts to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang sent Dao Lian to infiltrate the rebels under pretense of defection; they accepted him. He secretly circulated the government's reward schedule, and rebel leaders inside the city such as Li Jishu began to waver.

sentences.zh: 道連謀泄，為賊所殺，繼叔逾城出降，賊黨於是大離。

translations.literal: Dao Lian's plot was exposed and he was killed by the rebels; Jishu climbed over the wall and came out to surrender, and the rebel faction thereby greatly dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Lian's plot was discovered and he was killed; Jishu climbed over the wall to surrender, and the rebel faction fell apart.

sentences.zh: 乃四面進攻，沖車所沖，輒三五丈崩落。

translations.literal: Thereupon they attacked from four sides; where the battering rams struck, three to five zhang of wall would collapse.
translations.idiomatic: They then attacked from all sides; wherever the battering rams struck, thirty to fifty feet of wall collapsed.

sentences.zh: 時南門樓上擲下一級，並垂繩釣取外人，外人上，賊並放仗，雲向已斬順則，所投首是也。

translations.literal: At that time from atop the southern gate tower they threw down a head and also lowered ropes to fish up outsiders; when outsiders climbed up, the rebels all laid down their weapons, saying that Shunze had already been beheaded and the head thrown down was his.
translations.idiomatic: From the southern gate tower they threw down a head and lowered ropes to haul up outsiders; when men climbed up, the rebels laid down their arms, saying Shunze had already been beheaded and this was his head.

sentences.zh: 秦凱之走河北。

translations.literal: Qin Kaizhi fled to the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Kaizhi fled north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 斌坐滑臺退敗，免官。

translations.literal: Bin, on account of the retreat and defeat at Huatai, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was dismissed for the retreat and defeat at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 久之，復起為南平王鑠右軍長史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again raised up as Right Army Chief Clerk to Prince of Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was reappointed right army chief clerk to Prince of Nanping Shuo.

sentences.zh: 其後事蹟在《二凶傳》。

translations.literal: His later deeds are in the "Biographies of the Two Villains."
translations.idiomatic: His later career is recorded in the "Biographies of the Two Villains."

sentences.zh: 斌弟簡，歷位長沙內史。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Jian served in the post of Interior Minister of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Jian served as interior minister of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王誕為廣州，未之鎮，以簡為安南諮議參軍、南海太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guangling Dan was assigned to Guang Province but had not yet gone to his garrison, Jian was made Consulting Adjutant Pacifying the South and Administrator of Nanhai, acting in princely and provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Guangling Dan was assigned to Guangzhou but had not yet taken up his post, Jian was made consulting adjutant pacifying the south and administrator of Nanhai, acting in his stead.

sentences.zh: 東海王禕代誕，簡仍為前軍諮議，太守如故。

translations.literal: When Prince of Donghai Yi replaced Dan, Jian remained Consulting Adjutant to the Forward Army; his administrator post was as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Donghai Yi replaced Dan, Jian remained consulting adjutant to the forward army with his administrator post unchanged.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討元兇，遣輔國將軍、南海太守劉琬討簡，固守經時，城陷伏誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu entered to suppress the usurper, he sent General Assisting the State and Administrator of Nanhai Liu Wan to attack Jian; Jian held firm for a long time, but when the city fell he was executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to suppress the usurper, he sent General Assisting the State Liu Wan, administrator of Nanhai, against Jian. Jian held out for a long time, but when the city fell he was executed.

sentences.zh: 斌、簡諸子並誅滅。

translations.literal: The sons of Bin and Jian were all executed and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Bin and Jian were all executed.

sentences.zh: 劉延孫，彭城呂人，雍州刺史道產子也。

translations.literal: Liu Yansun was a man of Lü in Pengcheng and the son of the Inspector of Yong Province Liu Daochan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yansun was from Lü in Pengcheng and was the son of Yong governor Liu Daochan.

sentences.zh: 初為徐州主簿，舉秀才，彭城王義康司徒行參軍，尚書都官郎，為錢唐令，世祖撫軍、廣陵王誕北中郎中兵參軍、南清河太守。

translations.literal: He first served as Registrar of Xu Province, was recommended as a cultivated talent, became Acting Adjutant to the Minister of State under Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, and was made Magistrate of Qiantang; under Emperor Shizu's Pacification Army and Prince of Guangling Dan he was Central Army Adjutant of the Northern Army and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registrar of Xu Province, was recommended as a cultivated talent, served as acting adjutant to the minister of state under Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, and as gentleman of the ministry of revenue and magistrate of Qiantang; under the heir apparent's pacification army and Prince of Guangling Dan he was central army adjutant of the northern army and administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 世祖為徐州，補治中從事史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu was in Xu Province, he was appointed Acting Aide-de-Camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Xiaowu held Xu Province, Yansun was appointed his aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 時索虜圍縣瓠，分軍送所掠民口在汝陽，太祖詔世祖遣軍襲之，議者舉延孫為元帥，固辭無將用，舉劉泰之自代。

translations.literal: At that time the Northern Wei besieged Xuanhu and sent a detachment escorting captured common people to Ruyang. Emperor Taizu ordered Emperor Shizu to send troops to raid them; those in council nominated Yansun as commander-in-chief, but he firmly declined, saying he had no skill as a general, and recommended Liu Taizhi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei were besieging Xuanhu and had sent a detachment escorting captives to Ruyang. The emperor ordered the heir apparent to raid them; the council nominated Yansun as commander, but he firmly declined, claiming no military talent, and recommended Liu Taizhi in his place.

sentences.zh: 泰之既行，太祖大怒，免延孫官。

translations.literal: Once Taizhi had set out, Emperor Taizu was greatly angry and dismissed Yansun from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizhi departed, the emperor was furious and dismissed Yansun from office.

sentences.zh: 為世祖鎮軍北中郎中兵參軍，南中郎諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: He became Central Army Adjutant of the Northern Army under Emperor Shizu's Army Stabilizing the Realm, Consulting Adjutant to the Southern Commandant, and concurrently Chief Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He served as central army adjutant of the northern army under the heir apparent's Army Stabilizing the Realm, consulting adjutant to the southern commandant, and chief recorder.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐逆，府缺上佐，轉補長史、尋陽太守，行留府事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned against the usurper, the establishment lacked a senior aide; he was transferred to fill the post of Chief Clerk and Administrator of Xunyang, acting in the affairs of the remaining establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent marched against the usurper, his staff lacked a senior aide; Yansun was transferred to chief clerk and administrator of Xunyang, acting head of the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 三年，南兗州刺史竟陵王誕有罪，不受徵，延孫馳遣中兵參軍杜幼文率兵起討。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Inspector of Southern Yan Province, Prince of Jingling Dan, was guilty and did not accept the summons; Yansun urgently sent his Central Army Adjutant Du Youwen leading troops to raise the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince of Jingling Dan, governor of Southern Yan, refused the summons to court; Yansun urgently dispatched his central army adjutant Du Youwen with troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 既至，誕已閉城自守，乃還。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Dan had already closed the city and held it himself, so they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Dan had already shut the gates and held the city; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 誕遣使劉公泰齎書要之，延孫斬公泰，送首京邑。

translations.literal: Dan sent the envoy Liu Gongtai bearing a letter to win him over; Yansun beheaded Gongtai and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent Liu Gongtai with a letter to win him over; Yansun beheaded Gongtai and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 復遣幼文率軍渡江，受沈慶之節度。

translations.literal: He again sent Youwen leading the army across the river, under the command of Shen Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Youwen with troops across the Yangzi under Shen Qingzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 其年，進號車騎將軍，加散騎常侍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: That year he advanced in rank to General of the Cavalry and Chariots, was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to General of the Cavalry and Chariots, made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and granted a military band.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔延孫曰：「舊京樹親，由來常準。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict to Yansun said: "Planting kin in the old capital has always been the constant standard."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict to Yansun read: "Placing kinsmen in the old capital has always been our established practice."

sentences.zh: 卿前出所有別議，今此防久弭，當以還授小兒。

translations.literal: Your separate proposal when you went out before—now this defense has long been quieted and should be returned and entrusted to my young son.
translations.idiomatic: The separate arrangement you proposed when you left—now that this post has long been quiet, it should be returned to my young son.

sentences.zh: 」徵延孫為侍中、尚書左僕射，領護軍將軍。

translations.literal: " Yansun was summoned as Palace Attendant, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently General Protecting the Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Yansun was summoned as palace attendant, left vice minister of the masters of writing, and General Protecting the Army.

sentences.zh: 延孫疾病，不任拜起，上使於五城受封版，乘船自青谿至平昌門，仍入尚書下舍。

translations.literal: Yansun was ill and could not perform the bowing and rising; the emperor had him receive the enfeoffment patent at Wucheng, go by boat from Qingxi to Pingchang Gate, and then enter the lower quarters of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun was too ill to perform the obeisances; the emperor had him receive his patent of enfeoffment at Wucheng, travel by boat from Qingxi to Pingchang Gate, and take lodging in the masters of writing quarters.

sentences.zh: 又欲以代朱脩之為荊州，事未行，明年，卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished to have him replace Zhu Xiuzhi in Jing Province; the matter was not carried out. The next year he died, at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also planned to appoint him governor of Jing in place of Zhu Xiuzhi, but this was not carried out. The following year he died, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，下詔曰：「故侍中尚書左僕射、領護軍將軍東昌縣開國侯延孫，風局簡正，體識沈明，綢繆心膂，自蕃升朝，契闊唯舊，幾將二紀。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly regretted it and issued an edict saying: "The late Palace Attendant, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and General Protecting the Army, Marquis of Dongchang County, Yansun—his bearing was simple and upright, his substance and insight deep and clear. He was bound to the heart and backbone from his rise from the domains to court; our long partings and meetings were only old friendship, nearly two decades."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him and issued an edict: "The late palace attendant, left vice minister of the masters of writing, and General Protecting the Army, Marquis of Dongchang, Yansun—upright in bearing, deep in insight and judgment. Bound to us as a pillar of state from his days in the provinces to the capital, our bond of old friendship spanned nearly twenty years."

sentences.zh: 靈業中圮，則首贊宏圖；

translations.literal: When the imperial enterprise was mid-collapse, he was first to assist the grand design;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial house was in crisis, he was first to endorse the grand design;

sentences.zh: 義令既舉，則任均蕭、寇。

translations.literal: when righteous command was raised, his responsibility matched Xiao and Kou.
translations.idiomatic: when the righteous cause was raised, his responsibility matched that of Xiao He and Kou Xun.

sentences.zh: 器允棟幹，勳實佐時。

translations.literal: His capacity fulfilled the role of a pillar; his merit truly assisted the age.
translations.idiomatic: His capacity was that of a pillar of state; his merit truly served the times.

sentences.zh: 及累司馬兩官，出內尹牧，惠政茂課，著自民聽，忠謨令節，簡乎朕心。

translations.literal: When he accumulated the two offices of Chief Clerk, went out and in as intendant and governor, his benevolent government had lush achievements renowned among the people; his loyal counsel and fine integrity were plain in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Whether as chief clerk twice over or governing provinces within and without, his benevolent rule won renown among the people; his loyal counsel and fine integrity were plain to Our heart.

sentences.zh: 方燮和臺階，永毗國道，奄至薨殞，震慟兼深。

translations.literal: Just as he was to harmonize the terrace steps and forever assist the state's way, suddenly he reached death—shock and grief are both deep.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to harmonize the court and forever assist the state's course, he died suddenly—Our shock and grief are profound.

sentences.zh: 考終定典，宜盡哀敬。

translations.literal: Examining the end and fixing the rites, full mourning and respect are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of mourning should be observed with full respect.

sentences.zh: 可贈司徒，給班劍二十人，侍中、僕射、侯如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of State, granted twenty halberd-bearers, and Palace Attendant, Vice Minister, and Marquis remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He shall be posthumously made Minister of State, granted twenty halberd-bearers, with his posts as palace attendant, vice minister, and marquis unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏諡忠穆，詔為文穆。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices memorialized the posthumous title Zhongmu; the edict made it Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: " The responsible offices proposed the posthumous title Zhongmu; the edict changed it to Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「故司徒文穆公延孫，居身寡約，家素貧虛，每念清美，良深淒歎。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "The late Minister of State, Duke Wenmu, Yansun—he lived in few wants, his household was always poor and empty; whenever We recall his pure excellence, Our sighs of grief are truly deep."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "The late Minister of State, Duke Wenmu, Yansun lived modestly and his household was always poor; whenever We recall his integrity, Our grief is profound."

sentences.zh: 葬送資調，固當闕乏，可賜錢三十萬，米千斛。」

translations.literal: The resources for burial and sending-off will certainly be lacking; he may be granted three hundred thousand cash and a thousand hu of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Funds for his burial will surely be lacking; grant three hundred thousand cash and a thousand hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 子質嗣，太宗泰始中，有罪，國除。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded; in Taishi under Emperor Taizong he was guilty and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi succeeded him; in the Taishi era under Emperor Taizong he committed an offense and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 延孫弟延熙，義興太守，在孔覬傳。

translations.literal: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi was Administrator of Yixing; he is in the biography of Kong Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun's younger brother Yanxi was administrator of Yixing; his biography appears in that of Kong Xian.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：延孫接款蕃日，固出顏、袁矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yansun's reception of favor in his days in the domains was certainly above Yan and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Yansun's reception of favor during his years in the provinces clearly surpassed that of Yan Yanzhi and Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 風飆局力，又無等級可言，而隆名盛寵，必擇而後授，何哉？

translations.literal: In wind and storm, in scope of power, there was again no rank to speak of—yet lofty name and abundant favor had to be chosen before they were granted. Why?
translations.idiomatic: In talent and force of character he was not of the highest rank, yet lofty titles and abundant favor were granted only after careful selection. Why?

sentences.zh: 良以休運甫開，沈疾方被，雖宿恩內積，而安私外簡。

translations.literal: Truly because the age of rest had just opened and deep illness was just spreading—though old favor accumulated within, he was at ease in private matters and simple outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Because the dynasty's golden age had just begun and the emperor was still recovering from illness—though old affection ran deep within, outwardly Yansun was easy in private matters and restrained in demeanor.

sentences.zh: 夫侮因事狎，敬由近疏，疏必相思，狎必相厭，厭思一殊，榮禮自隔，遂得為一世宗臣，蓋由此也。

translations.literal: Insolence arises from familiarity in affairs; respect arises from nearness and distance. Distance surely brings mutual longing; familiarity surely brings mutual weariness. When weariness and longing differ in kind, glory and ritual naturally separate—thus he could become a pillar minister of an age; it was probably from this.
translations.idiomatic: Familiarity breeds contempt; respect arises from proper distance. Distance breeds longing; closeness breeds weariness. When weariness and longing pull apart, honor and ritual naturally keep their distance—thus he could stand as a pillar minister of his age. This is the reason.

sentences.zh: 子曰：「事君數，斯疏矣。

translations.literal: The Master said: "In serving one's lord, if one is frequent, one becomes distant."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "He who is importunate with his lord will end in estrangement."

sentences.zh: 」然乎！

translations.literal: " Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: " Is it not so!

sentences.zh: 然乎！

translations.literal: Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Is it not so!
